description: Testable research questions connecting ancient cannabis archaeochemistry, preservation, genomics, and modern analytical methods. No measured results or newly discovered cannabinoid identities are asserted.
doctrine: HYPOTHESIS ≠ OBSERVATION ≠ TENTATIVE_ANNOTATION ≠ CONFIRMED_IDENTITY ≠ OCCURRENCE ≠ BIOACTIVITY ≠ HUMAN_EFFECT ≠ SAFETY

sources.title: Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2,800 years ago
sources.role: Ancient botanical material and contested hair molecular signals; sequencing underway as stated in Bern's release.
sources.evidence_boundary: No assembled ancient cannabis genotype, variant calls, or full cannabinoid profile have been published in this source ledger.

sources.title: Cannabis was used as an intoxicant as early as 2,800 years ago
sources.role: Reports excellent DNA preservation and sequencing begun; no genetic sequence results yet.
sources.evidence_boundary: Announcement of ongoing sequencing is not evidence of specific synthase or thioesterase alleles.

sources.title: The origins of cannabis smoking: Chemical residue evidence from the first millennium BCE in the Pamirs
sources.role: Separate CBN-positive burning residues at Jirzankal and CBD, CBL, CBN in preserved Jiayi cannabis; one Jirzankal brazier also reported cannabivarin.
sources.evidence_boundary: Historical chemical signals do not demonstrate ancient relative potencies, novelty, or reliable original concentrations.

sources.title: Domesticated cannabinoid synthases amid a wild mosaic cannabis pangenome
sources.role: Reports genome structure diversity, relatively conserved THCAS/CBDAS, and ALT/BKR variation associated with THCV/CBDV.
sources.evidence_boundary: Correlations from modern genomes are not evidence that an ancient sample carried the relevant variants.

sources.title: Kendrick Mass Defect Filtering Enables High-Throughput Untargeted Annotation of Minor Phytocannabinoids
sources.role: Reports filtering of untargeted HRMS from 50 inflorescence samples, yielding 61 annotated phytocannabinoids across C1–C7 homologs and other families.
sources.evidence_boundary: Annotation is not necessarily isolation, standard confirmation, or new-compound identification.

sources.title: A MassQL-Based Framework for Rule-Guided MS/MS Class-Level Retrieval and Analog Discovery of Cannabinoids
sources.role: Demonstrates rule-based MS/MS class retrieval on public data, highlighting analog-like features missing from spectral libraries.
sources.evidence_boundary: Class-level matches are discovery candidates, not confirmed molecular structures.

sources.title: The novel heptyl phorolic acid cannabinoids content in different Cannabis sativa L. accessions
sources.role: Source of existing seven Candabiverse C7 provisional entries and their different statuses.
sources.evidence_boundary: CBGPA/CBCPA putative detection is distinct from other search targets not detected in this study.

sources.title: Large-scale whole-genome resequencing unravels the domestication history of Cannabis sativa
sources.role: Provides modern background in ancestry, domestication, and cannabinoid synthase selection.
sources.evidence_boundary: Modern population inference does not directly reconstruct prehistoric biochemistry.

hypotheses.title: Ancient genome comparison may reveal changes in precursor supply
hypotheses.basis: Tunnug seed DNA sequencing is underway; a modern cannabis pangenome associates ALT/BKR variation with rare varin-type cannabinoids.
hypotheses.prediction: When high-quality, authenticated ancient genotype data become available, comparison with modern references may identify ancestral states and differences in fatty-acid precursor-related loci.
hypotheses.disconfirming_observation: Ancient reads do not cover relevant loci or observed variants do not differ in ways that correlate with chemotype.
needed_data: Published authenticated ancient sequences and mapping quality
hypotheses.limits: This is an evolutionary research hypothesis. No ancient sequence data or new cannabinoids are identified here; genotype alone does not measure compound production.

hypotheses.title: Re-screen long-chain cannabinoid acid targets against current MS/MS evidence
hypotheses.basis: Cannabiverse already catalogs putative C7 acids CBGPA and CBCPA, and five not-detected search targets. Contemporary KMD and MassQL methods could audit them against independent modern spectra.
hypotheses.prediction: At least some candidate-family chemical signatures may be prioritized in independent datasets; authentic standard confirmation could distinguish real compounds from isomeric or instrument artifacts.
hypotheses.disconfirming_observation: No reproducible features survive blanks, retention-time validation, independently acquired MS/MS, or comparison to plausible isomers.
needed_data: Open peak tables or raw LC-HRMS/MS datasets with metadata
Orthogonal structural confirmation for putative hits
hypotheses.limits: Missing an entry in the 145-record atlas is not proof a compound is novel or naturally produced; no promotions to confirmed canon from mass matches alone.

hypotheses.title: Ancient preservation matrices create different cannabinoid observability profiles
hypotheses.basis: The 2019 study documents CBN in burned Jirzankal braziers and CBD/CBL/CBN in desiccated Jiayi material; 2026 Tunnug hair reports disputed CBN-consistent signals.
hypotheses.prediction: The same modern reference mixture may yield markedly different detectable chemical profiles in fresh, aged, heated, buried, and contamination-controlled matrices.
hypotheses.disconfirming_observation: Profiles show no repeatable matrix-associated differences beyond analytical noise and blank contamination.
needed_data: Matrix-specific negative controls and processing metadata
Independent controlled reference observations from appropriately equipped laboratories
hypotheses.limits: Do not back-calculate original THC potency or treat preservation products as automatically newly biosynthesized phytocannabinoids.

hypotheses.title: Kendrick homolog patterns and MassQL fragments can prioritize unknown features
hypotheses.basis: Peer-reviewed 2025 KMD and 2026 MassQL research provide complementary, interpretable discovery filters for homologous and structurally similar molecules.
hypotheses.prediction: A combined feature-ranking pipeline may flag reproducible cannabinoid-like signals that conventional reference-library matching misses.
hypotheses.disconfirming_observation: Ranked candidate features are fully explained by known adducts, isotopes, in-source fragments, degradation products, or contaminants.
needed_data: Open MS1/MS2 reference datasets with documented licenses
hypotheses.limits: A predicted match, molecular mass, graph edge, or structure proposal is never by itself a compound discovery.

hypotheses.title: Historical biomarker findings must be separated from clinical and natural-occurrence claims
hypotheses.basis: Ancient hair, funeral braziers, preserved botanical samples, and modern cannabis extracts carry different preservation, contamination, and identification constraints.
hypotheses.prediction: Explicit sample-matrix provenance and negative-control status will reduce false promotion of historical residue signals to naturally biosynthesized or medically active molecules.
hypotheses.disconfirming_observation: The ledger does not distinguish source matrices or independent assessment finds unresolved same-matrix contradictions.
needed_data: Source-specific controls, blanks, and sample metadata
Source quality review including competing interpretations
hypotheses.limits: No conclusions about clinical effect, safety, historical dosage, intentional use, or psychoactivity are drawn by the discovery ledger.
